comment: Professor Yellin is one of my favorite teachers at Richmond. He is so knowledgeable about his subjects and I feel like I've learned so much. His classes are extremely entertaining and I never feel bored. Participation is very important but he makes it easy to contribute with questions that are kind of common sense. His grading can be a little tough

Dr Yellin is a really funny and great professor. Though I only took FYS with him I really enjoyed the readings and the discussions we had in class. He is a tough grader but is clear on how to improve and how he can help his students.

Cannot say enough good things. During my freshman year I was going through a bit of a rough patch, and he was so understanding and helpful -- really made it feel like he cared about me and my success. Very passionate about American history, and did his best to keep students engaged and participatory. One of the reasons I'm a history major!

Capitalism and its Discontents was by no means an easy class, but Yellin is an outstanding professor who will really take the time to help you understand the complex readings. He grades harshly but his expectations, while high, are clear, and he gives you direct feedback to quickly improve. Fascinating class and Yellin is brilliant.

Dr. Yellin is very kind and enthusiastic as a professor. He obviously knows his material which makes class somewhat engaging. But by week 3 or 4 the full hour and 15 minute lectures get to be very repetitive and boring. I would be having a real hard time concentrating in his class after the first couple of weeks. Overall pretty solid but boring.

Professor Yellin is very clear on his expectations for assignments. That said, he is a very tough grader and very strict on deadlines, especially when it comes to papers. Also, if you take this class make sure you read and contribute every class (participation matters a lot).

I love Professor Yellin! He is very passionate about what he teaches and this makes class interesting, despite being online this year. He expects a lot of us as "historians", and so the writing for this class is not graded easily. But, if you pay attention and class and seek his feedback you should do just fine.

Capitalism and Its Discontents was great in terms of an FYS. Yellin assigned the most engaging readings of any of the professors that I had this year. He did a good job of making the curriculum interdisciplinary (econ, history, english, etc.). Always willing to talk and meet outside of class. Papers aren't easy but grading is fair.

Dr. Yellin is an amazing professor. He's incredibly intelligent, and his lectures are so in depth and fascinating. He's a tough grader, but that's because he expects a lot from his students. His comments on papers are very thoughtful and helpful, and he'll provide help through email or office hours. I would take him again in a heartbeat!

Makes you work hard, wants to see your blood, sweat, and tears, but he is always there to help you with any tasks. Papers are quite lengthy and topics are not straightforward, but all the assignments were really thought-provoking. Great historian, great pedagogic! Especially recommended for the FYS - will make you thrive through the rest of college

Dr. Yellin is the best professor that I had at UR thus far. He lectures are REALLY interesting and he's passionate about what he's teaching which makes the class even better. You will read a lot. He gives good feedback on papers and requires that students meet with him to for a big paper, i.e: the final. Definitely a great mentor! Take the class!

Dr. Yellin is probably the most intelligent and vibrant professor I've had so far at UR. He is an extremely nice guy who expects you to participate in class and won't hesitate to call you out if you try to slide through his class. Tough grader on papers but gives excellent feedback. Truly a genuine professor all around.
Great Professor. Very Helpful.
He is a smart man, but rather biased. He picks favorites, and sometimes tunes out certain comments/people. No one got an A in my class. It is hard to gauge his expectations.

Fantastic professor, really pushed students to engage with the material. His expectations  are high, but if you work hard you can do well, and he is extremely helpful! Definitely take a class with him if you can!
Rarely gives out A's. Is a very smart man, and gets very enthusiastic about class

He is a very passionate teacher, and his class on the Scottsboro Trials is very interesting. However, the class is difficult. He expects you to read everything, and assigns about 70 pages of reading for every class. The reading is usually fairly interesting, so it isn't that bad. He is a very interesting and smart professor- I would recommend him!

IMO, Yellin was not any more "unfair" in the way he grades writing than any other prof. in the history dept. at UR (they're all pretty tough).   He is a genuinely nice person who cares about the material and his students. If you have a question about a paper he will look at a draft with you.  Do the work, participate in class, and you will be fine.
Class is ridiculously boring, and he is unfair when he grades. NEVER EVER EVER take his class.

I have taken his 200,399 and 400. He isn't super easy by any means so if you're not a major then maybe not. BUT for majors, he has been amazing for research.  Basically, the American history classes he teaches have been super interesting-  they are complex but he is always crystal clear - you will improve as a writer - so go see him and you'll ACE!

Very enthusiastic and involved. Sometimes digs a little too deep into the books and makes it hard to answer questions. You really need to read and participate during class but he makes it easy and interesting. Not a lot of writing assignments and overall I actually liked core because of him.
I won't get his class if I were you.

Prof. Yellin is awesome!  He is willing to work with students outside of class and is genuinely a really nice person.  Grades a little tough on papers, but just because he expects a lot from his students.  He allows students to lead the class rather than lecturing.  Really funny and intelligent guy.

Not the best professor...he seems really nice at the beginning but then he grades you way too hard for a 100 level course. My best papers got horrible grades. Had to read 50+ pages per class and participation is 25%. He chose to help certain students and was harder on the ones that he expected more from. Way too much work for HIST100
Professor Yellin rocks. He knows as much about Woody Allen as he does about real history stuff. plus he's funny and cute.
